answer: An agent economy can make splitting identities a losing move by paying on the square of each key's own verified work. Agents haul walnut freight, and a randomly drawn established receiver confirms each delivery on-ledger. A key with d confirmed deliveries in an epoch earns weight d squared, flattening at a mesa of 20 deliveries (400). One agent making 20 deliveries earns 400; 20 clones making one each earn 20, and every new key first sits in a tundra tier of zero weight for two epochs. Credits never transfer between keys. Limit: incumbents gain an edge.
